info.title: Verification API
info.summary: Hosted and server-to-server identity verification: ID checks, liveness, face match, age, and credential verification.
info.description:
REST API for Verification APIs (`/api/v2`).

- **Hosted** — create a session with a `workflow_id`, redirect the user to the returned hosted `url`, receive a signed webhook on a terminal state, then pull the authoritative result from `GET /api/v2/session/{id}/decision`. The redirect-back `?status=` is a hint only — never treat it as final.
- **Standalone** — call individual check endpoints (`/api/v2/id-verification`, `/liveness`, `/face-match`, `/age-verification`, `/credential-verification`, `/kyc-credential`) directly for a synchronous result.

Successful responses are `{ success: true, data }` — there is no `error` key on success. Error responses are `{ success: false, data, error }` where `data` is `[]` (an empty array) or a populated object, never `null`. Authenticate with `X-API-Key: <App API key>` (a Bearer token with the same key is also accepted). API keys are created by a human in the Developer Portal — not via API.

All `/api/v2` routes are rate limited per client IP at ~150 requests/minute. A 429 body is `{ success: false, data: [], error: { code: "rate_limited", message } }` and carries no `Retry-After` header; successful responses include `X-RateLimit-Limit` / `X-RateLimit-Remaining`. POST endpoints accept an optional `Idempotency-Key` request header so a retry cannot double-run or double-charge.

tags.name: Sessions
tags.description: Hosted verification sessions and their decisions.

tags.name: Credentials
tags.description: Professional licence verification. **Always discover first:** GET /credential/states → pick a state → GET /credential/states/{state}/providers → take that provider's `provider_code` + `credential_name` and pass them to /credential-verification. Never hard-code a provider_code or guess a licence type — the board decides what it issues.

tags.name: Workflows
tags.description: Feature bundles for hosted sessions, managed via a full REST resource (`WorkflowController`). Create a workflow from a list of `features`, then pass its `id` as `workflow_id` when creating a session.

tags.name: Location
tags.description: Verify where the user actually is. What you send decides what you get back — send an expected point AND a radius to get a yes/no verdict; send neither to just capture the location.

tags.name: Identity
tags.description: Read back a previously-verified ("verify once, reuse") identity for a returning user, scoped to your project, without starting a new session.

post.description: Creates a hosted session and returns a Valyd-hosted `url` to redirect the user to. `workflow_id` is the UUID of a workflow (from the Developer Portal or the Workflows API) that selects the bundle of features to run. If you pass a `callback`, it must EXACTLY match an active, approved HTTPS webhook registered for the project, or you get 422 `callback_not_allowed`. Pass `valyd_access_token` to bind the session to a Managed-by-Valyd account.

get.description: Returns session summary objects newest-first (by `created_at`). This endpoint is NOT paginated: there is no cursor, page, or offset parameter and no total/next metadata. Use `limit` to cap the number returned (default 50; there is no server-enforced maximum). Narrow results with the `status` and `vendor_data` equality filters. `data` is an object with a `sessions` array.

parameters.name: vendor_data
parameters.description: Filter by your correlation ref (SDK arg `vendorData`).

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Max sessions to return (default 50; no cursor/offset/page pagination is available and no server-enforced maximum).

200.description: An object with a `sessions` array of session summaries, newest-first.

get.description: Fetch a session's current state (status, workflow, vendor_data, timestamps). Poll this while the user works through a hosted flow. For the OUTCOME of each check — and the identity — use GET /session/{id}/decision instead.

get.summary: Get full decision and per-check data
get.description: Returns the authoritative final decision plus the per-check breakdown. Call this after a terminal webhook to retrieve all extracted data.

patch.description: The manual-decision endpoint for a session that is currently `IN_REVIEW`. It only decides an IN_REVIEW session — calling it on any other state returns 409 `review_not_pending`. Setting `APPROVED` additionally requires that id_verification, liveness and face_match have all passed, otherwise you get 409 `required_face_checks_incomplete`. The decision is terminal and the session stops accepting further checks. It is an audited action.

status.description: REQUIRED. The terminal decision to force (e.g. APPROVED / DECLINED).

200.description: Updated session summary reflecting the decision.

get.description: On-demand read of a previously-verified ("verify once, reuse") identity, scoped to the calling project, without starting a new session. Look the record up by `valyd_id` (alias `pollus_id` — same value) OR by your own `vendor_data` — one of the two is REQUIRED; supplying neither returns 400 `missing_parameter`. Only an active record (not revoked, not expired) is returned; otherwise 404 `not_found`. The `identity` object carries a shareable `pseudonym`, `age_bands`, verified `licenses`, a `verified_at` timestamp and a `stale` flag — raw legal name and date of birth are never returned.

parameters.name: valyd_id
parameters.description: The user's public Valyd id. Provide this OR vendor_data. Alias: pollus_id (same value).

parameters.name: vendor_data
parameters.description: Your own correlation ref stored at verification time. Used when valyd_id is not supplied.

post.description: OCR + authenticity extraction from a government ID. Images may be sent as `multipart/form-data` files or as base64/data-URL strings in a JSON body of the same field names. Alternatively, pass `valyd_access_token` for ACCOUNT mode — the identity comes from the user's stored Valyd document and no `front_image` is required. A missing or unreadable image returns 400 `invalid_image`.

front_image.description: Front of the ID (file or base64). Required unless valyd_access_token is given.

back_image.description: Back of the ID, when applicable.

valyd_access_token.description: Optional. The user's Valyd access token → ACCOUNT mode: identity comes from the stored Valyd document, no document scan required.

post.description:
Passive liveness from a single selfie — proves a live person is present, NOT who they are (pair with /face-match for identity).

Passes when `live_score === 1`. A photo-of-a-photo, screen replay or print attack fails. No user action needed — nothing to blink or turn.

Send the frame straight from the camera at full quality: recompressing or downscaling destroys the very texture the check reads and causes false rejects. The selfie field is accepted as either `image` or `selfie`; file upload or base64/data-URL. Alternatively, pass `valyd_access_token` for ACCOUNT mode. A missing or unreadable image returns 400 `invalid_image`.

image.description: The selfie — file upload or base64. Full quality, straight from the camera. Alias: selfie.

valyd_access_token.description: Optional. The user's Valyd access token → ACCOUNT mode.

post.description: Issues a single-use, ~60-second liveness challenge for the anti-spoof and face-uniqueness burst flows. The server picks a random gesture; the client performs it while capturing the burst, then echoes the returned `challenge_id` back on the run. The challenge is consumed on first use and expires after `expires_in` seconds. No request body is required.

post.summary: Anti-spoof (is this a live human capture?)
post.description: Answers *is the submitted media a live human capture?* — not who it is. Send EITHER a single `image`/`selfie` (assurance "upload": single-frame passive analysis) OR `frames[]`, 3-8 chronological stills from a short camera burst (assurance "burst": per-frame voting + temporal sanity + same-face consistency). Files or base64/data-URL strings are both accepted. Returns a vendor-neutral `human_score` (0-100) in `check.data`; the check `score` carries the same value, and a single frame is capped at a lower confidence to steer integrators toward burst mode. Passing an optional `challenge_id` (from POST /antispoof/challenge) additionally requires the burst to show the commanded gesture. No image at all returns 400 `invalid_image`; more than 8 frames returns 400 `too_many_frames`. Requires the `antispoof` feature.

image.description: Single selfie — file or base64. Alias: selfie. Use frames[] instead for burst mode.

frames.description: 3-8 chronological burst stills (files or base64). Enables burst-assurance analysis. At most 8.

challenge_id.description: Optional. An id from POST /antispoof/challenge; the burst must then show the commanded gesture.

vendor_data.description: Optional. Your correlation ref, recorded on the audit session.

200.description: Anti-spoof result. `status` is `passed` for a live capture, `failed` otherwise; `check.data.human_score` is 0-100.

post.description: Runs the full anti-spoof pipeline and, ONLY if liveness passes, resolves the proven-live face against the global Valyd face gallery — returning the person's stable `valyd_` uuid and whether they were already known. If liveness fails, no identity lookup runs (and none is billed): the response is the anti-spoof result with no `identity`. On success, `check.data.identity` is `{ valyd_uuid, registered: "new"|"existing" }`; if the gallery lookup itself failed it is `{ error }`. Same media input as /antispoof (single `image`/`selfie` or 3-8 `frames[]`); strict-liveness projects must send a 3-8 frame burst (fewer returns 400 `frames_required`) and a satisfied `challenge_id`. Requires BOTH the `antispoof` and `face_uniqueness` features. Billed as anti-spoof + face_uniqueness.

image.description: Single selfie — file or base64. Alias: selfie. Use frames[] for burst mode.

frames.description: 3-8 chronological burst stills (files or base64). Required (min 3) for strict-liveness projects. At most 8.

challenge_id.description: Optional (required for strict-liveness projects). An id from POST /antispoof/challenge.

vendor_data.description: Optional. Your correlation ref; also used as the enrollment's external reference.

200.description: Anti-spoof result; on a live capture `check.data.identity` carries the resolved gallery uuid.

post.description:
1:1 face comparison: does the selfie show the same person as the reference portrait? Passes when similarity ≥ threshold (default ~0.95).

`image1` = the reference (e.g. the ID portrait). `image2` = the live selfie. Order matters only for reporting; the comparison is symmetric. Field aliases: `image1` accepts `id_image`, `image2` accepts `selfie`; files or base64/data-URL.

In ACCOUNT mode (`valyd_access_token`) send only the selfie — it is matched against the account's stored Valyd face vector, so no reference image is required.

This answers *same person?* — it does NOT prove the selfie is live. Pair it with /liveness to stop someone matching a photo of the ID holder.

Use the original, full-resolution images: a downscaled ID portrait is the most common cause of a false 'no match'. A missing or unreadable image returns 400 `invalid_image`.

image1.description: Reference portrait (e.g. the ID photo) — file or base64. Alias: id_image. Not required in account mode.

image2.description: The live selfie to compare — file or base64. Alias: selfie.

valyd_access_token.description: Optional. The user's Valyd access token → ACCOUNT mode: the selfie is matched against the stored Valyd face vector; image1 is not needed.

post.description: Enroll-or-match a face against the global Valyd face gallery: one face maps to one stable `valyd_uuid` across every integrator. Send a single `selfie`/`image` (single-click mode, single-frame liveness gate) OR `frames[]`, 3-8 chronological burst stills (live mode, the full anti-spoof pipeline gates enrollment). Files or base64/data-URL. The check passes whether the face is new or already known — read `check.data.registered` ("new" | "existing") and `check.data.valyd_uuid`; no similarity scores or liveness internals are exposed (`check.score` is null). Exactly 2 frames returns 400 `invalid_frames` (send 1 selfie, or 3-8 frames); more than 8 returns 400 `too_many_frames`; strict-liveness projects require a 3-8 frame burst (fewer returns 400 `frames_required`) and a satisfied `challenge_id`. Requires the `face_uniqueness` feature.

selfie.description: Single selfie — file or base64. Alias: image. Single-click mode.

frames.description: 3-8 chronological burst stills for live verification (files or base64). Exactly 2 is rejected. At most 8.

external_ref.description: Optional. Your own reference to associate with this face's enrollment.

challenge_id.description: Optional (required for strict-liveness projects). An id from POST /antispoof/challenge.

vendor_data.description: Optional. Your correlation ref, recorded on the audit session.

parameters.name: valyd_uuid
parameters.description: The gallery face id to forget.

delete.description: Removes THIS project's link to a gallery face id. The project's active enrollment is marked unlinked; if the id is a shadow identity with no remaining active enrollments, its template and vector are hard-deleted. Returns `{ valyd_uuid, unlinked: true, deleted }`, where `deleted` is true only when the underlying identity was fully removed. 404 `not_found` when the id is unknown or this project has no active enrollment for it. Requires the `face_uniqueness` feature.

200.description: The project's link to the face id was removed.

post.description:
Computes the age from a date of birth and answers the age bands you ask for. Returns `data.age` plus a `data.bands` map — one entry per band you requested.

**Bands are flexible:** `"18"`, `18`, `"18+"` and `"is_18_plus"` all mean the same thing. Each answer is `{ satisfied: true|false, min_age }` (`verified` is emitted as a deprecated alias of `satisfied`); an unparseable band comes back `{ satisfied: null, error: "unknown_band" }`.

`status` is `passed` only when EVERY requested band is satisfied — ask for one band if you want one verdict.

Fresh mode (a raw `dob`) can answer ANY band, including odd ones like `"20"`. In ACCOUNT mode (`valyd_access_token` / `valyd_id`) NO `dob` is sent — the bands are derived from the account's stored DOB, and the response is `data: { source: "account", bands }` with no `age`/`dob`; an account with no stored DOB returns 422 `account_dob_unavailable`. Account mode answers only the canonical thresholds (16/18/21/30/65).

dob.description: REQUIRED in fresh mode (omit in account mode). Date of birth, ISO preferred (YYYY-MM-DD, e.g. 1990-04-12).

bands.description: Optional. Bands to assert. Accepts "18" / 18 / "18+" / "is_18_plus". Defaults to is_18_plus if omitted.

valyd_access_token.description: Optional. The user's Valyd access token → ACCOUNT mode: bands are derived from the account's stored DOB; do not send `dob`.

post.description:
One endpoint, and **what you send decides what you get**:

**1. No name → SEARCH (details).** You ask "what's on file for this licence number?". We skip identity matching and return the board's record: `mode: "search"`, `found: true`, **`match: null`**. A finding is NOT proof the licence belongs to anyone — never treat it as a verification.

**2. Name → VERIFY.** The identity agent runs and matches your name against the board record: `mode: "verify"`, `match: true`/`false`. A wrong name fails even when the number is right.

**3. `valyd_access_token` → ACCOUNT mode.** We resolve the account from the token and match against its **verified KYC name**. Any name you send is IGNORED — so an integrator cannot claim someone else's licence. Returns proofs, and badges the licence on the account.

**Always discover first** (GET /credential/states → /credential/states/{state}/providers) and pass the selected `provider_code` + `credential_name`. `license_state` + the licence number are always required.

Live board lookups take 10–60s — use a generous timeout. Send the number exactly as the board writes it (e.g. `TL.0011377`, not `TL0011377`).

first_name.description: Optional. Use with last_name instead of full_name.

last_name.description: Optional. Use with first_name instead of full_name.

full_name.description: OPTIONAL — it is the mode switch. Omit → search (details back, match null). Send → verify (agent matches this name). Ignored in account mode. Alternative: first_name + last_name.

license_type.description: The provider's `credential_name` from the providers list (e.g. "Medical Doctor"). Required unless you send provider_code.

license_state.description: REQUIRED. 2-letter state code from GET /credential/states (e.g. CO). Alias: state.

license_number.description: REQUIRED. Exactly as the board writes it, punctuation included (e.g. TL.0011377). Alias: license_no.

npi.description: Optional NPI, when the provider supports it.

provider_code.description: The provider's `provider_code` from the providers list. Pins the exact board — strongly recommended, no guessing.

valyd_access_token.description: Optional. The user's Valyd access token → ACCOUNT mode: identity comes from their verified KYC name and any name you send is ignored.

post.description: ID verification + liveness + face match + license lookup in one call. The license is matched against the name OCR'd from the ID (never client-supplied), preventing impersonation. Returns `data` = { session_id, status, checks[] } only — raw name/dob are deliberately NOT echoed. Images accept a file upload or a base64/data-URL string.

front_image.description: Front of the ID (file or base64).

selfie.description: Live selfie for liveness + face match (file or base64).

provider_code.description: Optional. Pins the exact board (alias of license_type).

get.description:
**Step 1 of licence verification.** Lists every state/jurisdiction that has at least one licence provider wired up.
Take a `state_code` from here and pass it to /credential/states/{state}/providers to see what that board actually issues.

SDK: `verify.credentials.states()` → `[{ stateName, stateCode, providerCount, mappingCount }]`.

**Step 2 — this is where `provider_code` comes from.** Lists what the state board issues. Show these as your "licence type" dropdown, then pass the SELECTED entry straight through to /credential-verification:

- `provider_code` → send as `provider_code` (pins the exact board, no guessing)
- `credential_name` → send as `license_type` (what the board calls it, e.g. "Medical Doctor")
- `required_fields` → the inputs you must collect for this provider (e.g. `license_no`, `remote_code`)

Key the dropdown on `credential_code`, NOT `provider_code`: one provider serves many credentials, so provider_code is not unique per row.

SDK: `verify.credentials.providers(stateCode)` → `[{ providerCode, providerDisplayName, credentialCode, credentialName, stateCode, remoteCode, requiredFields }]`.

post.description: Bundles a set of `features` into a reusable workflow. Pass the returned workflow `id` as `workflow_id` when creating a hosted session. Adding `age` without `id_verification` auto-injects `id_verification`.

get.description: List your workflows — the reusable feature bundles a hosted session runs. Returns `data: { workflows: [...] }`; pass a workflow `id` as `workflow_id` when creating a session.
Fetch one workflow: its features and configuration. Returns `data: { workflow: {...} }`.

patch.description: Update a workflow's features or settings. Applies to sessions created AFTER the change — sessions already running keep the pipeline they started with.

delete.description: Delete a workflow. Sessions already created with it keep working; new sessions can no longer reference it.

post.description:
Send the captured GPS point. **What you send decides what you get back — there are exactly three modes:**

**1. Expected point + `radius_m` → you get a VERDICT.** You asked "is this person at the place?", so we answer it: `status: passed` when inside the radius, `status: failed` when outside (the failure message says how far off they were). `data.match` is `true`/`false`, `data.distance_m` is the distance.

**2. Expected point but NO `radius_m` → no verdict, just the distance.** No threshold was given, so we cannot judge: `status: passed` and `data.match` is **`null`**. You get `data.distance_m` and decide yourself what "close enough" means. Do not read `passed` here as "they are at the place" — it only means the capture worked.

**3. No expected point at all → capture-only.** `status: passed` and we hand the location straight back as-is: `latitude`, `longitude`, `accuracy`. `data.match` is `null`. Use this when you just want to record where they were.

A real fix is always mandatory: blocked permission or missing coordinates is a hard `failed` — never a pass. Coordinates are PII: they appear only in the check `data` and are never logged.

accuracy.description: Reported GPS accuracy radius in metres. Optional — echoed back so you can judge how trustworthy the fix is.

expected_latitude.description: Optional. The place they are supposed to be. Send WITH expected_longitude to enable modes 1/2. Omit for capture-only.

expected_longitude.description: Optional. Pairs with expected_latitude — both are needed; one alone is ignored.

radius_m.description: Optional. How close counts as "there", in metres. **Only with a radius do you get a true/false verdict** (mode 1). Without it, match is null and you only get distance_m (mode 2).

200.description: Check ran. Read `status` + `data.match` per the three modes above.

score.description: The distance in metres, when an expected point was given.

distance_m.description: Metres from the expected point (only when one was given).

radius_m.description: Echoes what you sent; null when you gave no radius.

match.description: true/false only in mode 1. **null** in modes 2 and 3 — no threshold was given, so no verdict was made.

post.description: Valyd POSTs this to your app-level or per-session `callback` URL when a session reaches a terminal state. Verify the signature before trusting it: the `X-Valyd-Signature` header is the lowercase hex `HMAC-SHA256` of `"{timestamp}.{rawBody}"` keyed by your webhook signing secret. Reject timestamps older than 300s and dedupe on `X-Valyd-Event-Id`. The webhook is a notification only — call the decision endpoint for full data.

parameters.name: X-Valyd-Timestamp
parameters.description: Unix seconds when the event was signed.

parameters.name: X-Valyd-Event-Id
parameters.description: Unique event id; equals body `event_id`. Use for idempotency.

2XX.description: Return any 2xx quickly to acknowledge. Non-2xx is retried with exponential backoff.

apiKeyAuth.name: X-API-Key
apiKeyAuth.description: Your App API key from the Developer Portal.

bearerAuth.description: The same App API key may be sent as a Bearer token.

LicenseBadge.description: A normalised verified-licence badge. Empty fields are dropped, so any field may be absent.

IdentityRecord.description: A reusable verified identity as returned to integrators — pseudonym + proofs only, never raw legal name or date of birth.

valyd_id.description: The user's public Valyd id (the user's uuid).

pseudonym.description: Stable, shareable pseudonymous handle resolved from the identity core; null if the user has none.

verified_at.description: When the identity was verified / last refreshed (ISO 8601).

stale.description: true when the cached identity-core source changed and the integrator should re-verify.

CaptureEnv.description: Optional client-declared capture environment. When `virtual_suspect` is true a virtual camera (OBS / ManyCam / etc.) is assumed and the check fails closed with signal `virtual_camera`. Client-declared: a tampered client can omit or falsify it, so it only catches the honest virtual-camera case.

virtual_suspect.description: The client's judgement that the camera stream came from a virtual / injected device.

camera_label.description: The device label the client observed (truncated to 120 chars in the failure record).

AntispoofCheck.description: The anti-spoof check result. `score` carries the same 0-100 human_score as `data.human_score`.

assurance.description: "upload" for a single image, "burst" for a 3-8 frame sequence.

challenge.description: The commanded gesture, present when a challenge_id was supplied.

challenge_performed.description: Whether the burst showed the commanded gesture (present only when a challenge was required).

signal.description: Machine-readable failure reason on a failed check (e.g. spoof_detected, no_face, virtual_camera).

identity.description: Present ONLY on POST /antispoof/identity, and only when liveness passed: the resolved gallery identity — { valyd_uuid, registered } on success, or { error } if the gallery lookup failed.

registered.description: Whether the face was newly enrolled or already known.

error.description: Human-readable failure reason, or null on pass.

AntispoofEnvelope.description: Synchronous anti-spoof response. `data.check` carries the anti-spoof result.

challenge_id.description: Opaque single-use id to echo back on the run as challenge_id.

challenge.description: The gesture the burst must show.

FaceUniquenessCheck.description: The face-uniqueness check result. `score` is always null — no similarity score is exposed.

valyd_uuid.description: Stable global face id — the same value for this face across every integrator.

registered.description: "new" if the face was just enrolled, "existing" if already in the gallery.

binding.description: "binding" — the enrollment was written to the live gallery.

code.description: Machine-readable failure code on a failed check (e.g. no_face, uniqueness_failed).

error.description: Human-readable failure reason, or null on pass.

FaceUniquenessEnvelope.description: Synchronous face-uniqueness response. `data.check` carries the result.

deleted.description: true only when the underlying (shadow) identity had no other active links and was hard-deleted.

SessionStatus.description: APPROVED, DECLINED, ABANDONED, and EXPIRED are terminal (a webhook is sent).

CheckStatus.description: Lifecycle: pending → running → passed | failed | review. statuses.md lists only the three terminal values; hosted.md adds pending/running.

data.description: Empty array `[]` on most errors, or a populated object for some codes (e.g. `review_not_pending` returns `{ status }`). Never null.

workflow_id.description: REQUIRED. The UUID of the workflow (feature bundle) to run, from the Developer Portal or the Workflows API.

valyd_access_token.description: Optional. Binds the session to a Managed-by-Valyd account. sso/reuse workflows require it — a missing token on those returns 401 `valyd_login_required`.

redirect_url.description: Where Valyd redirects the user's browser after the flow.

vendor_data.description: Your internal correlation ref; echoed on webhooks and the decision.

url.description: Hosted capture URL to redirect the user to.

SessionEnvelope.description: Success envelope — success responses carry only `success` + `data` (no `error` key).

SessionSummary.description: The session summary shape returned by list, get, decision-status and update-status. It has NO `url` or `session_token`.

decision.description: Terminal decision status string, or null while not decided.

data.description: Per-check details; shape varies by check type.

valyd_id.description: Linked Valyd account id, or null for a fresh (non-Valyd) session.

decision.description: The final decision as a single status string (e.g. "APPROVED"), normalised from the session decision.

verifications.description: Per-check outcomes keyed by check type.

identity.description: Verified profile + licenses for a Valyd-linked session; null otherwise.

StandaloneEnvelope.description: Synchronous standalone-check response. `data.check` carries the single check result.

Workflow.description: A reusable feature bundle for hosted sessions.

features.description: Enabled features (from `config('verify.features')`, e.g. id_verification, liveness, face_match, age, credential, location, antispoof, face_uniqueness).

REQUIRED. At least one feature. Each value must be one of `config('verify.features')` (id_verification, liveness, face_match, age, credential, location, antispoof, face_uniqueness, …). Adding `age` without `id_verification` auto-injects id_verification.

event_id.description: Equals the X-Valyd-Event-Id header; dedupe key.

decision.description: A short status string (e.g. "approved"), consistent with the decision API which now returns `decision` as a single status string. [owner: confirm the exact webhook payload against the queue-worker dispatcher (idp-queue.service) before relying on an object form.]

MissingParameter.description: A required query parameter was not supplied.

FeatureNotAllowed.description: The feature this endpoint needs is not enabled for the project.

error.message: Feature 'antispoof' is not enabled for this project.

LivenessBadRequest.description: The submitted capture was rejected before scoring. Codes: `invalid_image` (no image/frames), `too_many_frames` (more than 8 frames), `invalid_frames` (exactly 2 frames on face-uniqueness), `frames_required` (a strict-liveness project needs a 3-8 frame burst), `challenge_required` / `challenge_expired` (the challenge_id was missing, already used, or expired).

error.message: Provide `image` (file or base64) or `frames[]` (3-8 burst stills).

ValidationError.description: Malformed body or missing required field.

InvalidApiKey.description: Missing or invalid API key. A completely missing key uses code `API_KEY_MISSING` ('API key is required. Provide X-API-Key or Authorization: Bearer.'); an invalid key uses `invalid_api_key`.

error.message: API key is required. Provide X-API-Key or Authorization: Bearer.

NotFound.description: Session or resource does not exist.

WorkflowNotFound.description: The referenced workflow_id does not exist for this project.

CallbackNotAllowed.description: The `callback` URL does not exactly match an active, approved HTTPS webhook registered for the project.

error.message: Callback URL is not an approved webhook for this project.

BillingRequired.description: Billing could not cover the requested session/checks.

ReviewConflict.description: The session is not in a state that can be decided. `review_not_pending` (session is not IN_REVIEW) returns `data: { status }`; `required_face_checks_incomplete` is returned when approving before id_verification, liveness and face_match have all passed.

InvalidImage.description: A required image was missing or could not be read.

AccountDobUnavailable.description: Account mode was requested but the resolved Valyd account has no stored date of birth.

error.message: Account has no stored date of birth.

RateLimited.description: Rate limit exceeded. All `/api/v2` routes are throttled per client IP at ~150 requests/minute. The 429 body carries NO `Retry-After` or `X-RateLimit-*` headers.
